newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy discusses terrorism with Iran.
newsitem.headline: Italy discusses terrorism with Iran.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini met his Iranian counterpart Ali Akbar Velayati for talks on Tuesday and said he hoped Iran would increasingly distance itself from what he called international terrorism.

"Italy raised, with special reference to international terrorism, the most constructive positions recently adopted in Iran's public declarations and it hoped that those continue with ever-increasing determination towards a decisive distancing from this phenomenon," the Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
Dini told Velayati that Italy intended to continue along the route of "critical dialogue" begun by the European Union "to favour the gradual reintegration of (Iran) in international relations".

Europe's position contrasts with that of the United States, which has urged the international community to isolate Iran, contending it plays host to Islamic fundamentalists bent on destabilising governments in North Africa and the Middle East.
Dini said Italian firms also had a strong interest in Iran, an important energy supplier for Italy.

The meeting was hotly criticised by Iranian anti-government groups. "To shake the hand of an official representative of the clerical-terrorist dictatorship which dominates Iran contradicts the fundamental principles of human rights," the National Council of Iranian Resistance said in a statement.

An Iranian human rights group, the Comitato Mohammad Hossein Naghdi, also condemned Italy for hosting what it termed "the representative of a state which has made terror and terrorism its raison d'etre".
